// diagnostic

E0501

Empty `[]` needs a context type

What

Empty `[]` needs a context type

Why

The registered sema rule applies here

Fix

Follow the guidance for E0501

Worked example

First UI snapshot mentioning E0501: tests/ui/carrier_partial_not_kept.stderr.

Error [E2417]: explicit failure domain ``ImportErr`` is not an Error type
  --> tests/ui/carrier_partial_not_kept.jet:7:32
    |
  7 | fn import_rows(rows: [String]) [String] !ImportErr -> {
    |                                ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
 Why: A `!` contract may name `Err`, a Core error, a type marked `#Error`, an all-error union, or `Never`; arbitrary value types do not describe failures.
 Fix: use a Core error, add `#Error` to a local error type, or remove the explicit error contract.
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E2417

Error [E0501]: an empty list needs a type
  --> tests/ui/carrier_partial_not_kept.jet:13:27
    |
 13 |     spotty :: import_rows([String]{})
    |                           ^^^^^^^^^^
 Why: write `[]` only where the list type is already known from around it
 Fix: name the element type on the literal: `[Int].{}`
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E0501

Error [E2402]: `?` can't convert `ImportErr` into `Err` — no declared conversion exists
  --> tests/ui/carrier_partial_not_kept.jet:13:15
    |
 13 |     spotty :: import_rows([String]{})
    |               ^^^^^^^^^^^
 Why: `?` uses the declared conversion rail; `ImportErr` can reach `Err` only through `impl ImportErr -> Err`
 Fix: add `impl ImportErr -> Err { … }` before this function, or change the return type
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E2402
